title: workflow-state.json
description: PO-agent resumable session state — written by workflow-state.sh, read by po-agent and the session-status hook. One file per GitHub issue at specs/<key>-<slug>/workflow-state-<issue>.json (per-issue isolation, #173). The PO-agent (GAP-006 / #32) is the sole writer in production; build-implement-tdd performs a narrow guarded patch on task completion.

repo.description: GitHub repository in owner/name form, e.g. 'macatocz/my-app'.

branch.description: Active feature branch name at session start.

worktree_path.description: Absolute path to the git worktree for this run, or null when working in the main checkout. Set by the PO-agent worktree-lifecycle helper (GAP-017 / #46) at session start before any sub-agent dispatch; cleared back to null when the worktree is removed on successful completion.

worktree_retained.description: True when the worktree has been deliberately retained on disk after a HALT (GAP-017 / #46). The PO-agent does NOT remove a retained worktree on cleanup; a human operator (or GAP-016 / #45 rebase logic) inspects it. Steady-state value is false.

worktree_retain_reason.description: Short reason string explaining why the worktree was retained (e.g. a HALT code such as 'HALT-003' or a free-form marker like 'merge_conflict' set by resolve-pr-conflict). Paired with worktree_retained=true. Null when worktree_retained is false.

issue_number.description: GitHub Issue number this run is driving.

sub_tasks.description: Ordered list of implementation sub-tasks derived from plan.md. PO-agent is the sole writer.

id.description: 1-based task index matching TASK_INDEX in build-implement-tdd.

phase.description: Implementation mode for this task, or null before plan analysis.

agent_result.description: The R1 envelope object returned by the coder agent for this task, or null before dispatch.

current_phase.description: High-level pipeline phase the run is currently in (e.g. 'refine', 'implement', 'verify', 'pr', 'done'). Null before first dispatch.

resume_point.description: Opaque hint for the session-status hook — identifies where to resume (e.g. 'task:3', 'build-verify', 'pr-comments'). Null when not resumable.

budget_consumed_tokens.description: Cumulative token count consumed by this run, updated after each sub-agent dispatch. Never reset — the daily/per-task cost ceilings (HALT-007) evaluate against this cumulative total.

session_baseline_tokens.description: Value of budget_consumed_tokens at the start of the current session (#281). HALT-007B evaluates the context-window pressure against the delta (budget_consumed_tokens - session_baseline_tokens), NOT the cumulative total, so a resumed session starts its context budget fresh. Set to budget_consumed_tokens on every HALT-007B handoff; 0 at init. Distinct from budget_limit_tokens/HALT-007, which stay cumulative for cost control. Optional for backward compatibility with in-flight state files predating #281 — readers default it to 0 when absent.

budget_limit_tokens.description: Hard token ceiling for this run. When budget_consumed_tokens >= budget_limit_tokens the kill-switch fires HALT-007 (cost control — applies needs-human-review).

context_warn_tokens.description: Soft context-window threshold (GAP-004 / #30 extension). When budget_consumed_tokens >= context_warn_tokens at an outer-loop boundary, the proactive handoff path fires HALT-007B — checkpoint, summarise, self-restart. Distinct from budget_limit_tokens: this is a quality control (avoid context-window degradation around 170 k), not a cost control. Default 150000; operators on 200 k models may raise to 180000.

outer_iteration.description: How many outer-loop iterations have completed. HALT-008 fires when this reaches 3.

merge_conflict_cycles.description: Count of merge-conflict resolution attempts within this run (GAP-016 / #45). Incremented by resolve-pr-conflict on every irreconcilable conflict (Step 6 HALT path). HALT-008 fires when this reaches MAKATO_MAX_MERGE_CONFLICT_CYCLES (default 3) — separate ceiling from the outer_iteration counter so a single run can exhaust re-plan budget AND conflict-resolution budget independently.

ci_failure_cycles.description: Count of completed CI repair rounds returned by build-fix-ci. The PO-agent mirrors this result, never increments it for polling. Default repair limit is disabled (MAKATO_MAX_CI_FAILURE_CYCLES=0); a positive explicit ceiling returns CI_REPAIR_LIMIT. Private PR-scoped checkpoints preserve progress across sessions.

structural_halt_cycles.description: Durable cross-run counter of how many separate PO-agent runs on THIS issue terminated on a structural HALT (#347, epic #319). Incremented exactly once per run that ends on a structural-HALT code — the authoritative classification set is HALT-003 (structural blocker), HALT-STRUCTURAL, HALT-008 with data.origin == 'outer_iteration' (re-plan budget exhausted), and HALT-010. It is NOT incremented on non-structural terminations: HALT-007 (cost), HALT-007B (context handoff), or HALT-008 with origin merge_conflict/ci_failure. Distinct from outer_iteration (a within-run re-plan counter reset per run) — this is the cross-run recurrence property AC-epic-1 of #319 requires to make 'repeated structural failure on the same issue' detectable. NEVER reset on a HALT-007B context handoff: the resumed session must read the same value the prior session persisted. Initialised to 0 at init. Optional for backward compatibility with in-flight state files predating #347 — readers default it to 0 when absent.

reshape_cycles.description: Durable cross-run counter of how many makato-plan reshape attempts have been dispatched for THIS issue by _reshape_pass in loop.sh (#350, epic #319). Incremented by the loop's reshape pass on each successful decompose+to-issues dispatch. When reshape_cycles >= MAKATO_MAX_RESHAPE_CYCLES (default 3) the reshape pass stops dispatching and applies needs-human-review. Initialised to 0 at init (or treated as 0 when absent for backward compatibility). Optional for workflow-state files created before #350.

halt_audit.description: Immutable append-only log of HALT events. Each entry is written when a HALT code fires. Each code's `origin`/`retryable` classification values are defined in `plugins/makato-orchestrate/halt-conditions.md` § *HALT classification table*.

ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with millisecond precision when the HALT fired.

data.description: HALT-code-specific context payload. Shape varies per code — consumers must tolerate unknown keys.

retryable.description: Whether the autonomous loop can auto-retry once the triggering condition resolves, without operator intervention. True for transient/auto origins (e.g. HALT-007B context handoff, HALT-012 reviewer-timeout); false for human-origin HALTs requiring operator judgement. Absent on legacy entries — consumers must default-false when missing.

origin.description: Who must act to unblock this HALT. 'auto' = fully automated (loop handles it, no human needed — e.g. HALT-007B self-restart); 'transient' = condition may resolve without human action but is not guaranteed (e.g. HALT-012 waiting for a reviewer); 'human' = operator judgement required (e.g. HALT-003 structural blocker). The loop gates `needs-human-review` on this field: only 'human' origin entries trigger the label; 'auto' and 'transient' do not. Absent on legacy entries — consumers must treat missing as 'human' to preserve backward-compatible label behaviour.

retry_after_secs.description: Optional hint for 'transient' and 'auto' paths: suggested wait in seconds before the loop re-attempts. Only meaningful when retryable is true. Absent when not applicable (e.g. 'human' origin HALTs or when no specific wait is suggested).

human_review_cycles.description: Count of times the issue was labelled needs-human-review during this run.

github_pr_number.description: GitHub PR number opened by this run, or null before build-create-pr succeeds.

progress_comment_id.description: GitHub issue-comment ID of the single 'live' progress comment maintained for the driven issue (human-readable run narration, best-effort). Null before the first progress-comment.sh call creates it. Written only via shared/progress-comment.sh through the workflow-state.sh patch layer; both the loop guard and PO-agent use that single path. Losing or resetting it (e.g. GitHub outage) only starts a fresh follow-up comment — never blocks the run or fires a HALT.

lessons_learned.description: Append-only log of structured observations collected during the run (GAP-015 / #37). PO-agent appends after every outer-loop cycle event — CI fix, CHANGES_REQUESTED address, HALT trigger, or sensor fix resolution. The recall-lessons subcommand reads these across prior workflows for the same repo and injects the top-3 most-recent into the dispatch bundle of a fresh PO-agent session, so the next run starts warm.

ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with millisecond precision when the lesson was appended.

cycle.description: Outer-loop iteration count at the moment the lesson was recorded (mirrors workflow-state.outer_iteration). 0 is valid for lessons recorded before the first re-plan.

trigger.description: What kind of event the lesson captures. ci_failure: PR CI checks turned RED; halt: a HALT-* code fired (including HALT-STRUCTURAL); review_comment: reviewer applied CHANGES_REQUESTED; sensor: a sensor finding (lint/typecheck/security) prompted a fix; merge_conflict: resolve-pr-conflict gave up after rebase + merge -X ours (GAP-016 / #45).

description.description: Structured one-line summary of what happened. Per AC technical notes, keep under 200 chars — structured, not narrative. Helper truncates with a '…' suffix if the caller exceeds the cap rather than rejecting.

files_affected.description: Repo-relative paths the cycle touched (e.g. coder fix targets, sensor finding paths, conflict paths). Empty array when not applicable.

tier.description: Optional persistence tier for a captured lesson. Semantic facts route to semantic memory; procedural patterns route to procedural memory.

tags.description: Optional tags retained with this lesson in durable memory.

bundle.description: Optional skill/language/framework domain tag for this lesson (e.g. 'python', 'infra', 'ci'). Used by recall-lessons --bundles filter (#470). Absent on legacy entries without a bundle.

scope.description: Optional breadth classification: generalizable applies across issues; local is specific to this issue. Used by recall-lessons sorting.

occurrences.description: Optional count of how many times this pattern has been observed. Higher values sort earlier within the same scope level.

label.description: Optional free-form label tag complementary to bundle (e.g. a GitHub label name). Used by recall-lessons --labels filter (#470).

session_summary.description: ≤ 500-token handoff summary produced by the context-summariser sub-agent (GAP-004 / #30 extension). Injected as the first user message in the fresh session after a context-ceiling handoff. Null before the first handoff. The 4000-char cap is a defensive upper bound — the agent's system prompt enforces the 500-token budget; this just rejects pathological inputs.

session_count.description: How many context-ceiling handoffs this run has performed (GAP-004 / #30 extension). Incremented by context-handoff.sh after each successful self-restart. When session_count >= MAKATO_MAX_HANDOFFS (default 5) the proactive handoff path is disabled and HALT-007 fires instead — prevents infinite restart loops.

handoff_reason.description: Why the previous session ended (GAP-004 / #30 extension). 'context_ceiling' marks a clean handoff initiated by HALT-007B; the fresh session injects session_summary and resumes from resume_point. Null when no handoff is in flight. The session-status hook (GAP-007 follow-up) reads this field to decide whether to print the '↻ context handoff in progress' banner.

restart_failed.description: Set true by context-handoff.sh when the self-restart subprocess could not be spawned (e.g. 'claude' binary not on PATH), OR when the check-pid liveness watchdog (#284) determines a spawned resume subprocess died after fork or never acknowledged startup within MAKATO_HANDOFF_ACK_TIMEOUT. Triggers the HALT-007 fallback path — the issue is labelled needs-human-review and the run terminates. False in steady state.

spawned_pid.description: PID of the detached resume subprocess spawned by the HALT-007B context-handoff self-restart (#284). Written by context-handoff.sh immediately after the nohup fork, before disown, so the check-pid liveness watchdog can probe it with `kill -0`. Cleared back to null by check-pid once the resumed session confirms startup (resume_ack present and fresh). Optional for backward compatibility with state files predating #284 — readers treat an absent field as null (no handoff subprocess to supervise).

last_session_id.description: Claude session UUID of the most recent autonomous dispatch for this issue (#616). Written by loop.sh:cmd_dispatch after the dispatch child exits, extracted from the terminal {"type":"result",...} stream-json line of the dispatch log. This UUID — NOT the spec KEY or issue number — is the value `claude --resume` requires. Both loop.sh:_stall_resume and context-handoff.sh:_emit_resume read it to re-enter the session; when absent (hard crash before the terminal result line, or a legacy state file) they skip resume / fall back to HALT-007 respectively rather than pass an invalid KEY to --resume. Overwritten on every dispatch so it always reflects the latest session. Null at init. Optional for backward compatibility — readers treat an absent field as null.

resume_ack.description: ISO-8601 timestamp (millisecond precision) written by the po-agent as its first action on resuming from a context_ceiling handoff (#284), BEFORE it clears handoff_reason. Signals that the detached resume subprocess started successfully and reached the po-agent resume path. The check-pid watchdog treats resume_ack fresher than the latest HALT-007B halt_audit entry as proof of life. Null at init and between handoffs. Optional for backward compatibility — readers treat an absent field as null.

design_decision.description: Append-only log of design-time decisions captured during the run (#603). Records chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and rationale so design intent survives context handoffs. Written by workflow-state.sh append-decision; read by po-agent and grill-with-docs. Optional field — absent on state files created before #603; readers default to an empty array.

id.description: Short ISO-timestamp slug uniquely identifying this decision entry, e.g. '20260803T110700Z'. Generated by append-decision at write time.

ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with millisecond precision when the decision was recorded.

title.description: Short title for the decision (e.g. 'Use jq patch over Python script for state writes').

chosen.description: Description of the approach that was selected.

rejected.description: List of alternative approaches that were considered and rejected.

rationale.description: Why the chosen approach was selected over the alternatives.

source.description: Optional: origin of this decision entry — e.g. 'build-refine', 'grill-with-docs', or a file path such as 'docs/decisions/adr-001.md'.

plan_analysis.description: Output of plan-analyst stored in workflow-state so build-verify Gate 4 can read it without re-running plan-analyst. Written by build-implement-tdd after plan-analyst dispatch (Step 4). Optional — absent on state files created before #581; readers treat null/absent as 'gate non-mandatory' (backward compat).

tracer_required.description: True when plan-analyst determined that the change spans multiple architectural layers and a tracer-bullet approach is warranted. When true, build-verify Gate 4 treats the integration suite as mandatory (blocking failure instead of advisory).

layers_detected.description: List of architectural layer names detected by plan-analyst for this story (e.g. ['api', 'service', 'persistence']). Informational — Gate 4 uses distinct_layer_count for the numeric threshold.

distinct_layer_count.description: Number of distinct architectural layers detected (length of layers_detected). Build-verify Gate 4 treats the integration suite as mandatory when this value is >= 3, regardless of tracer_required.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the file was first created via the init subcommand.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent write. Automatically updated by write/patch/append-lesson.

issue_trace_id.description: SHA-256 hex digest of concat(repo, issue_number) minted at init time; stable across all sessions (incl. HALT-007B handoffs) for the same issue; optional for backward compat — absent fields read as null.
